request: Hoist the three independent epic-heading grammar declarations (roadmap/parse.mjs EPIC_HEADING_RE, roadmap-sync/sync.mjs EPIC_HEADING, roadmap-sync/append.mjs EPIC_HEADING) into one canonical module under .claude/skills/lib/, and move assertInert with it so the CWE-74 title-forgery guard sits at the canonical site.
novelty_evidence: No spec chapter, roadmap item, or backlog entry derives this. Searched .claude/memory/backlog/ for 'epic.heading', 'EPIC_HEADING' and 'heading grammar' -> zero matches. It originates as a /simplify flagged row at 1aed0ae ('out-of-scope refactor, belongs in a new spec') plus the 'Out of scope / Noted' section of docs/archive/2026-08-15/epic-roadmap-and-backlog-retriage/security.md. Partial pattern precedent exists for the PLACEMENT only: .claude/skills/lib/argv.mjs is an established cross-skill shared module. The grammar merge itself has no precedent, because the three regexes accept different inputs (parse.mjs matches with '## ' stripped; the other two require the prefix) and return different captures, so unifying them is a behaviour decision rather than a copy.
track_reason: Heavier than the leanest track (tdd-quickfix) by one written artifact and one gate. Justified because the three regexes are not interchangeable: the shared grammar's contract (does it accept a raw line or a stripped heading; does it return number, title, or both) is a design call that silently changes what standup/gather.mjs reports as shipped if chosen wrong. The spec records that contract for review BEFORE six call sites are rewired to it. User confirmed spec-entry over tdd-quickfix via AskUserQuestion.
